prediction.likelyOutcome: BlueRoad is very likely to recover materially more than Piedmont's $48,700 deposit and more than the baseline's narrow $146,100-$292,200 estimate, because its expert's before-value testimony survived the Daubert challenge and the auction sale provides real (if contestable) after-value evidence of substantial severance damage tied to loss of event-area access. But full recovery of the ~$14M theoretical diminution is unlikely given the forced-sale character of the auction, Gibson's failure to provide an independent after-value appraisal, and Piedmont's credible (and partially admission-supported, partially contradicted) access-retention defense; expect a jury verdict in the low-to-mid seven figures, substantially above the direct-take floor but well below BlueRoad's theoretical maximum.

issues.label: Severance/Incidental Damages via Before- and After-Taking Valuation

figures.label: Gibson (BlueRoad expert) before-taking value
figures.quote: Mr. Gibson prepared an appraisal in which he reached the conclusion that the property’s value before the taking was $25,500,000.

figures.label: Turner (Piedmont expert) before-taking value
figures.quote: BlueRoad questioned Mr. Turner regarding his before-taking valuation of $11,792,800 (as of October 2019)

figures.label: Farrell (owner) lay opinion of before-taking value
figures.quote: I believed at the time of the take, it was worth approximately $26 million dollars.

figures.label: 2022 auction sale price (BlueRoad's after-value proxy)
figures.quote: BlueRoad sold the property at auction in 2022 in six separate parcels for a total of $11,500,000.

issues.label: Direct Damages for the Taken Easement Strip

figures.label: Direct damages for right-of-way land (Turner)
figures.quote: As to the land used for the easement itself, the right-of-way, Mr. Turner opined that the direct damages were $98,700.

figures.label: Piedmont's deposit already paid
figures.quote: $48,700, which was deposited with the circuit court clerk

outcome.description: The Davidson County jury (August 2024) found a before-taking value of $25,500,000 and an after-taking value of $11,603,200, i.e. incidental damages of $13,896,800; judgment was entered for $13,798,100 after crediting Piedmont's $98,700 deposit, plus $14,203 discretionary costs. The Tennessee Court of Appeals affirmed on April 1, 2026, upholding admission of the owner's before-only appraisal and the jury's blending of the two experts' values. Amount used is the total compensation found (the deposit is part of it).
outcome.finalNote: Affirmed; judgment of $13,798,100 is the $13,896,800 verdict net of the $98,700 already deposited.
